# PILOT SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Pilot Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 1 November 2026 (the "Effective Date") between Larkspur Data Systems, Inc., a fictional company with offices at 400 Weir Street, Suite 12, Port Halden ("Provider"), and Fernhill Community Dental Group, a fictional practice with offices at 18 Orchard Row, Port Halden ("Customer"). Provider and Customer are each a "Party".

## 1. Definitions

1.1 "Platform" means Provider's hosted appointment-scheduling and recall software, including its web dashboard, the patient reminder service and the related documentation.

1.2 "Customer Data" means data that Customer or its staff submit to the Platform, including patient contact details and appointment records.

1.3 "Order Form" means the ordering document signed by both Parties that references this Agreement, which may list the number of locations, users and the Fees.

1.4 "Business Day" means a day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in Port Halden.

## 2. Services

2.1 Provider will make the Platform available to Customer for up to three (3) practice locations and twenty-five (25) named users during the Term.

2.2 Provider will provide onboarding assistance consisting of one data import from Customer's existing scheduling system and two remote training sessions of up to ninety (90) minutes each.

2.3 Support is available by email on Business Days between 8:00 and 18:00 local time. Provider will use reasonable efforts to respond to support requests within one Business Day.

2.4 Provider may update the Platform from time to time, provided that updates do not materially reduce the functionality described in the documentation.

## 3. Pilot Term

3.1 The pilot term begins on the Effective Date and continues for three (3) months (the "Pilot Term").

3.2 During the Pilot Term the Parties will meet at least once a month to review adoption and the success criteria listed in the Order Form.

3.3 Customer may end the pilot for convenience at any time during the Pilot Term on fourteen (14) days' written notice under Section 12. Fees paid for the Pilot Term are not refundable.

## 4. Fees and Payment

4.1 Customer will pay a one-time pilot fee of USD 1,500 for the Pilot Term, invoiced on the Effective Date.

4.2 For any Renewal Term (as defined in Section 10), Customer will pay a subscription fee of USD 1,150 per practice location per month, invoiced annually in advance on the first day of that Renewal Term.

4.3 Invoices are due within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Overdue amounts bear interest at one percent (1%) per month or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less.

4.4 Fees exclude taxes. Customer is responsible for any sales, use or similar taxes, other than taxes on Provider's income.

4.5 Provider may increase the subscription fee for a Renewal Term by up to seven percent (7%) by giving Customer written notice at least thirty (30) days before that Renewal Term begins.

## 5. Customer Responsibilities

5.1 Customer is responsible for the accuracy of Customer Data and for obtaining any consents required to send appointment reminders to its patients.

5.2 Customer will keep user credentials confidential and will promptly notify Provider of any unauthorized use of the Platform.

5.3 Customer will not resell the Platform, attempt to reverse engineer it, or use it to send messages unrelated to patient scheduling.

## 6. Data Protection

6.1 Provider will process Customer Data only to provide the Platform and support, and in accordance with Customer's documented instructions.

6.2 Provider will maintain administrative, technical and physical safeguards appropriate to the nature of Customer Data, including encryption of Customer Data in transit and at rest.

6.3 Provider will notify Customer without undue delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours, after becoming aware of a breach of security affecting Customer Data.

6.4 Within thirty (30) days after this Agreement ends, Provider will make Customer Data available for export and will then delete it, except for copies it must retain by law.

## 7. Confidentiality

7.1 "Confidential Information" means non-public information disclosed by one Party to the other that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential. Customer Data is Customer's Confidential Information.

7.2 The receiving Party will use the disclosing Party's Confidential Information only to perform under this Agreement and will protect it with at least reasonable care.

7.3 These obligations do not apply to information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving Party, that the receiving Party already knew without restriction, or that it develops independently.

7.4 The obligations in this Section 7 continue for three (3) years after this Agreement ends, and for Customer Data, for as long as Provider holds it.

## 8. Warranties and Disclaimers

8.1 Provider warrants that the Platform will perform materially in accordance with its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is for Provider to correct the non-conformity or, if it cannot do so within thirty (30) days, for Customer to terminate the affected services and receive a refund of prepaid fees for the remainder of the then-current term.

8.2 Except as stated in Section 8.1, the Platform is provided "as is", and each Party disclaims all other warranties to the extent permitted by law.

## 9. Limitation of Liability

9.1 Neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental or consequential damages, or for lost profits, arising out of this Agreement.

9.2 Each Party's total liability arising out of this Agreement will not exceed the Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve (12) months before the event giving rise to the claim.

9.3 Sections 9.1 and 9.2 do not limit liability for breach of Section 7 or for a Party's fraud or wilful misconduct.

## 10. Continuation of Services

10.1 Customer's staff and patients rely on uninterrupted reminders, so the Parties intend that service continue without a gap at the end of the pilot.

10.2 At the end of the Pilot Term, this Agreement will continue for an additional term of twelve (12) months (a "Renewal Term") unless either Party gives the other written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days before the last day of the Pilot Term. Each Renewal Term will be followed by a further Renewal Term of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives such notice at least sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Renewal Term.

10.3 The Pilot Term together with any Renewal Terms is the "Term".

## 11. Termination

11.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement on written notice if the other Party materially breaches it and does not cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving notice describing it.

11.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other Party becomes insolvent or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors.

11.3 Except as stated in Sections 3.3, 8.1 and 11.1, Customer may not terminate this Agreement during a Renewal Term, and Fees for the remainder of a Renewal Term remain payable.

11.4 Sections 4 (for unpaid Fees), 6.4, 7, 9, 12 and 13 survive the end of this Agreement.

## 12. Notices

12.1 Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective when received.

12.2 Notices to Provider must be delivered by hand, by courier, or by certified mail to: Legal Department, Larkspur Data Systems, Inc., 400 Weir Street, Suite 12, Port Halden. Notices to Customer must be sent to the address on the first page of this Agreement, attention: Practice Manager.

12.3 Email to Provider's support or account management addresses does not constitute notice under this Agreement, but Provider will accept notices of non-renewal sent by email to legal@larkspur.example if Provider confirms receipt in writing.

12.4 Either Party may change its notice address by notice to the other.

## 13. General

13.1 Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other's consent, except to a successor to substantially all of its business on notice.

13.2 Neither Party is liable for delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, provided it uses reasonable efforts to resume performance.

13.3 This Agreement, together with the Order Form, is the entire agreement between the Parties about its subject matter. If the Order Form conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls unless the Order Form expressly states otherwise.

13.4 Any amendment must be in writing and signed by both Parties.

13.5 If any provision is found unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in effect.
